question: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, $f(x) = x^3$. Is $f$ an equivalence relation if we define $xRy \iff f(x) = f(y)$? Justify.
explanation: Yes, $R$ is an equivalence relation because $f(x) = f(y)$ is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive (as equality is an equivalence relation).

options.A: Yes, $R$ is an equivalence relation because equality of function values is reflexive, symmetric and transitive
options.B: No, $R$ is not reflexive because $f(x)\neq f(x)$ for some real $x$
options.C: No, $R$ is not symmetric because $f(x)=f(y)$ does not imply $f(y)=f(x)$
options.D: No, $R$ is not transitive because $f(x)=f(y)$ and $f(y)=f(z)$ never imply $f(x)=f(z)$
